sources.entry: Sesame - Open-source app that indexes the dashboards, reports, sites, PRs, and files Claude Code and Codex delivered, and reopens them when you type or say a few words. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/qiwei66/sesame) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: Sesame is a macOS app and Claude Code plugin that builds a local library of the dashboards, reports, sites, files and PRs your AI assistant produced, and reopens them from a few typed or spoken words.
summary.what_it_does: Sesame scans your existing Claude Code and Codex session history on first launch and counts every artifact the AI delivered, including dashboards, reports, decks, sites, files and pull requests. It keeps this index on your Mac and lets you type a few words, or hold a hot key and speak, to get the artifact itself rather than the chat it came from. If several items match, it shows a short list; if none match, it says so. Results are opened with the return key, and it can fall back to a wider search when nothing local fits. The README also describes an optional model for disambiguation, and a Claude Code plugin that exposes three MCP tools (search_artifacts, open_artifact, artifact_stats) so Claude can look up and open artifacts in a conversation. A share card showing only counts can be generated from the first-run panel.
use_cases: find a dashboard I built with Claude Code last week
reopen a report or deck generated by an AI assistant
locate files or pull requests created in old AI chats
let Claude Code open an earlier artifact from a prompt
index local Claude and Codex history without uploading it
how_to_run: claude plugin marketplace add qiwei66/sesame && claude plugin install sesame@sesame
notable: Opens the artifact itself (dashboard, file, site, PR) rather than the chat that produced it
Local-only index in ~/Library/Application Support/Sesame; never uploaded, and never writes to ~/.claude or ~/.codex
Hold-to-talk voice search via a configurable hot key (default ⌥⇧Space)
Works as an MCP server and Claude Code plugin with search_artifacts, open_artifact and artifact_stats tools
Installs via Homebrew with ad-hoc signing, so no Apple Developer account is needed
caveats: Requires macOS 13 or later; the first install compiles the app from source and takes a few minutes
Needs Node.js 22.18+ and the Xcode Command Line Tools
Reads only Claude Code and Codex history, so other AI tools are not indexed
The optional model sends your sentence and candidate titles, types and keywords to the configured model; in Claude Code, matched titles, types, links and times go to that conversation's model
